newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPGs soften amid a lack of buyers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPGs soften amid a lack of buyers.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices softened Friday, as large trading companies stayed out of the market, players said.
Mont Belvieu, Texas, propane was traded at 36.25 cents a gallon, a quarter cent lower than Thursday's high trade.
"Propane has lost some steam," said one Houston trader. He expected to see material deals to go down to 36.00 cents later in the day.
Another Houston player said he expected the market to "soften up a tad if the big players stay out of the market."
Belvieu deals in butane and isobutane were done at, or just below, Thursday's bid prices. Butane was done at 43.50 cents and isobutane at 46.50 cents.
Ethane and ethane mix traded in Belvieu at 21.75 cents and 20.75 cents respectively.
Deals were also bearish in the Conway, Kansas, market. Propane there sold for 36.00 cents and 36.13 cents. Butane, retreating to its mid-week price, sold for 40.50 cents.
Meanwhile, both natural gasoline and ethane values were about a half cent softer in Conway.
Players in both hubs said many traders were taking half-days, or were on vacation. --Tim Gardner, New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1632 --
